rules.rationale: Long SMILES tracks large polar surface and H-bonding burden, lowering lipophilicity in the ESOL transfer prior.
Very long strings indicate extended polar functionality that should depress logD more strongly than the long bin.
Moderate hetero atom count is compatible with retained hydrophobic surface, so penalty is partly offset.
Aromatic ring density raises LogP, the dominant driver of the lipophilicity objective here.

skills.hypothesis: Source size and donor effects invert onto lipophilicity: long, hetero-rich strings lose logD while aromatic, halogen-rich scaffolds gain. Fails if aromatic_high co-occurs with heavy hetero loading.

rules.rationale: Source ring_bin gave the strongest effect; high ring token density should raise lipophilicity.
Intermediate ring count carries weaker positive signal consistent with partial source transfer.
Counter to source rotatable-bond transfer: heavy branching often adds polar substituents that reduce logD here.
Absence of halogens removes a known lipophilicity contributor, so such molecules are downweighted.

skills.hypothesis: Ring rigidity transfer is positive but branching transfer may reverse under lipophilicity, where polar branch groups are common. Fails if halogen-free polar aromatics are actually high logD.

fixed_initial.lesson: Source solubility effects on size and donor count invert sign for lipophilicity; aromatic and halogen content transfer positively, so size and hetero penalties must be paired with scaffold-hydrophobicity gains.
fixed_initial.revision_summary: Kept the successful size/donor transfer as hydrophobic_burden_transfer and added ring_rigidity_counter_hypothesis reversing the uncertain branch/rotatable-bond relation; selected the transferred size-driven skill for deployment.

rules.rationale: Longest SMILES in the ESOL transfer carried the largest negative size effect; heavy polar appendages depress logD.
Dense aromatic carbocyclic surface adds nonpolar pi area, the most reliable positive lipophilicity driver.
Moderate halogenation enlarges hydrophobic surface and lowers desolvation cost, raising logD.
Heavy heteroatom loading adds hydrogen-bonding and desolvation cost that opposes lipophilicity.

skills.hypothesis: Retains the well-calibrated size penalty and aromatic gain, adds a mild polarity penalty. The smiles_long penalty is dropped entirely because it covered most of the pool and dragged on weak seeds. Fails if long scaffolds dominate the top tail.

rules.rationale: Aromatic carbon surface stays the mechanistically safest positive term across chemotypes.
Heavily halogenated scaffolds are the classic high-logD chemotype, a small distinctive subset.
Reverses the positive rotatable-bond transfer: heavy branching often adds polar substituents that lower logD.
Few double bonds co-occur with saturated polar functionality, weakly opposing measured lipophilicity.

skills.hypothesis: Counter-hypothesis: the low-confidence smiles_length and ring/branch transfers are downweighted in favor of halogen and heteroatom polarity balance. Fails if heteroatom-rich aromatics still score highest.

true_feedback.lesson: Across both generations the size-penalty-plus-aromatic skill calibrated more consistently than counter-hypotheses, but the broad smiles_long penalty was the main drag on its weakest seeds and the polarity terms were better folded into a single mild negative.
true_feedback.revision_summary: Kept the transfer family but dropped the over-broad smiles_long penalty, folding polarity into one hetero_high term so only the extremely long bin is penalized. Replaced the counter-hypothesis with a branch-reversal and double-bond-polarity variant grounded in the rotatable-bond transfer, and deployed the refined transfer skill on its better mean calibration AUC.

rules.rationale: Short SMILES were the most soluble ESOL bin; small polar molecules partition poorly into octanol, so invert that sign.
Long strings carried the largest negative solubility effect; logD is anti-correlated with logS, so bulk should raise lipophilicity.
Dense aromatic carbon surface is the classic mechanistic driver of octanol-water partitioning in drug-like molecules.
Halogens add polarizable hydrophobic surface without hydrogen-bond donors, reliably increasing measured logD.

skills.hypothesis: Source solubility effects transfer with inverted sign: size bins that hurt solubility should help lipophilicity, reinforced by aromatic and halogen surface. Fails if long SMILES encode polar heteroatom chains rather than hydrophobic bulk.

rules.rationale: Abundant N/O heteroatoms add hydrogen bonding and desolvation cost, directly suppressing octanol-water partitioning.
Heteroatom-poor, carbon-rich frameworks maximize nonpolar surface and partition strongly into the organic phase.
Heavy halogenation is a robust lipophilicity enhancer, independent of any source solubility evidence.
Counter to the low-support rotatable-bond-to-branch transfer: branched alkyl substitution adds hydrophobic bulk, not polarity.

skills.hypothesis: Polarity composition, not string length, controls logD; the donor-to-heteroatom and rotatable-to-branch transfers are downweighted or reversed. Fails if hetero_low and halogen_high bins are too small and structurally atypical.

no_feedback.lesson: ESOL-to-lipophilicity transfer needs sign inversion because logD opposes logS; also, conditions must be plain field-to-value maps, and weight should not be spent on bins covering half the pool.
no_feedback.revision_summary: Rewrote both skills into the required single-field conditions format, trimmed the dominant smiles_long weight while keeping the inverted short-SMILES penalty grounded in source evidence, retained mechanistic aromatic/halogen domain terms, kept the polarity counter-hypothesis that reverses the low-support rotatable-bond-to-branch relation with lower semantic mass, and deployed the inversion skill.

rules.rationale: Fused ring density adds rigid hydrophobic surface; the source ring role also carried the largest transfer weight.
Halogens add polarizable, weakly solvated surface; their absence removes a standard logD contributor.
Halogenated aromatics are the classic high-logD motif, combining ring hydrophobicity with halogen surface effects.
Dense heteroatoms raise hydrogen bonding and desolvation cost, the usual mechanism depressing measured logD.

skills.hypothesis: Rigid halogenated aromatic scaffolds with few heteroatoms maximize lipophilicity. Fails if halogen bins mark polar heteroaryl halides or if ring-dense candidates are simultaneously hetero-saturated, collapsing the two positive rules.

rules.rationale: Reverses the source rotatable-bond transfer: branch tokens often mark alkyl substituents adding hydrophobic surface.
Aromatic carbon frameworks with few heteroatoms are the most hydrophobic combination available in this catalog.
Heteroatom loading adds polarity and desolvation penalty, the dominant loss channel for logD.
Downweights the uncertain halogen relation: halogen_none covers over half the library and may carry little signal.

skills.hypothesis: Tests that carbon-rich, low-heteroatom aromatics with alkyl branching drive logD while halogen absence is near-neutral. Fails if branching mostly marks polar amide or sulfonamide side chains.

shuffled_feedback.lesson: Across two development generations the ring/halogen scaffold family scored highest, while inverted source size priors underperformed; heteroatom density looks like a more defensible penalty than branching, but sixteen seeds cannot establish mechanism.
shuffled_feedback.revision_summary: Retained the leading scaffold skill but replaced its weak branching penalty with a heteroatom-density penalty shared by the runner-up, and slightly raised semantic mass. The counter-hypothesis now reverses the branching relation and explicitly downweights the broad halogen_none penalty. Deployed the scaffold skill.
